candidate.body: When a note was edited outside the CLI, rebuild the index instead of editing canonical notes, then verify with doctor and search.
do_not_use_when: The term is missing from the note body itself (the note is wrong, not the index); fix it through the CLI update path instead.
Semantic search is the thing failing; rebuild only refreshes the FTS index.
done_when: doctor shows index fresh with no problems and search returns the edited note at its current revision.
candidate.fallback: If rebuild reports issues or the term still does not appear, stop, do not edit canonical notes, and report the rebuild output and doctor output to the user.
steps: Run doctor and note index state; run search for the new term and note the result and relevance flag.
Run rebuild (no name) to refresh the index for the domain; expect ok with an indexed count.
Run doctor again and confirm index is fresh with empty problems.
Run search for the new term and confirm the note appears with its current revision; a body-only term may still show relevant:false, which is the relevance gate, not an index gap.
candidate.title: Repair stale search index after out-of-CLI note edit
use_when: A note body was changed outside the CLI and a term from the new text does not retrieve the note; doctor or search shows an index mismatch.

candidate.body: Before applying a plan that edits an existing note, compare the plan expected_revision with the note current revision. If they differ, do not apply; report the plan as stale and leave the store unchanged.
done_when: Either the plan was applied with doctor and validate clean, or it was refused as stale with the note unchanged and doctor and validate clean.
candidate.fallback: If inspect-plan or read is unavailable, do not apply the plan; report that the revision could not be verified.
steps: Run inspect-plan <plan_id> and note expected_revision for the target effect.
Run read <note_id> and compare its revision field with expected_revision.
If they differ, do not run apply. Note that the plan is stale and that its diff may regress newer content.
If they match, run apply and then doctor and validate to confirm consistency.

candidate.body: When doctor reports a pending_recovery operation after an interrupted write, inspect its journal and complete it forward with the CLI recover command, then verify.
do_not_use_when: the journal effect is unclear, or the target files changed since the journal was written (recover then refuses or the content is not the one intended); use backward or --abandon only after reviewing the diff
the operation is a capture or other kind whose effects you have not inspected
done_when: doctor shows pending_recovery [] and the operation is committed in history, with the target file holding the journal after-content
candidate.fallback: If recover fails or the target changed, do not force it. Leave the operation pending, run diff OPID to inspect, and report to the user; use recover OPID --abandon only with their approval.
steps: Run doctor and read pending_recovery and warnings; run history to find the operation ID and state.
Read .operations/OPID/journal.json and check each effect: path, before, after. Confirm the intended result is the after-state.
Run recover OPID --direction forward. Expect state committed.
Verify: run doctor (pending_recovery must be empty), history (state committed), and read the effect path for the expected content.
candidate.title: Complete an interrupted Living Memory operation forward
use_when: doctor reports pending_recovery with an operation ID, and the operation journal shows a planned effect whose after-state is the intended result

candidate.body: Recover one deleted canonical note from backups/ using restore-plan, reviewing the plan before apply so no other note is removed.
done_when: read and search return the restored note, doctor and validate are clean, and the note count is the pre-restore count plus the restored notes.
candidate.fallback: If apply fails or the plan shows deletes, do not force it; run CMD doctor and CMD history, and recover with recover OPERATION if an operation is pending. Use CMD undo PLAN/OPERATION to reverse an applied restore.
steps: Confirm the note is missing: run search and read for its title; check that INDEX.md still lists it.

List the zip entries (System.IO.Compression.ZipFile in PowerShell) and confirm the note file is inside, e.g. domains/demo/notes/KNOWLEDGE - <slug>-<id8>.md. Read it only through the zip; do not extract into the store.
Run: CMD restore-plan <path-to-zip>. Require summary delete:0 and write equal to the number of missing notes; if delete is nonzero, stop and find out why before applying.
Run: CMD inspect-plan <PLAN_ID>. Confirm the diff only adds the missing file.
Verify: CMD doctor (problems empty), CMD validate (issues empty), CMD read and CMD search for the title.
candidate.title: Restore a deleted canonical note from a backup zip
use_when: A canonical note is missing from domains/DOMAIN/notes but its backup zip exists under backups/ in the store root.
